open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark marked_at
open_points.question: Which authority supplies the instant written to `marked_at` when the first publication mark is created?
options: An instant supplied by the calling flow
open_points.default_guess: Use an injected UTC system clock owned by the service.

witness.initial: A placement exists without a publication mark, and the calling flow has just received a Portal photo id.
events: The calling flow asks the deliverer to record the publication.
The service creates the first PublicationMark.
outcomes: One implementation writes the instant from its injected system clock.
Another implementation writes the database server's current time.
witness.observer: An operator or test reading the stored PublicationMark sees different `marked_at` values.

open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark marked_at
open_points.question: In which representation is `marked_at` stored and compared: timezone-aware UTC, UTC without an offset, or another representation?

witness.initial: The service is ready to create a first publication mark at 2026-11-21T10:00:00Z.
events: The calling flow records the publication.
witness.observer: Persistence code, migrations, and tests see different values and comparison rules.

open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark marked_at
open_points.text: The calling flow reports the `photo_id` right after `photo.publish` answers, and the deliverer creates the mark.
open_points.question: What event does `marked_at` denote: receipt of the request, creation of the record, successful persistence, or some other boundary?
options: Instant the record-publication request is accepted
Instant immediately before the mark is inserted
Instant at which the transaction commits successfully
open_points.default_guess: Use the instant immediately before inserting the mark in the successful transaction.

witness.initial: A record-publication request begins, then waits before its transaction commits.
events: The calling flow submits the Portal photo id.
The request waits for a persistence lock.
The transaction writes and commits the mark.
outcomes: One implementation records the request-start instant.
Another records an instant immediately before the eventual write.
witness.observer: An operator comparing request logs with the stored mark sees materially different publication times.

open_points.subject: record-publication operation
open_points.text: The same `photo_id` again returns the first mark; another `photo_id` is refused.
open_points.question: How many clock readings may one record-publication operation take, including retries, and must a replay or refusal read the clock at all?
options: Exactly one reading only when a new mark is created
One reading at the start of every call
A fresh reading for every transaction attempt
open_points.default_guess: Read the clock exactly once, only for the successful creation of a new mark; replays and refusals do not read it.

witness.initial: No mark exists, and the first insert attempt encounters a retryable transaction conflict.
events: The calling flow asks to record a publication.
The service reads the clock and attempts the transaction.
The transaction retries after the clock advances.
outcomes: One implementation preserves the first reading across the retry.
Another reads again and stores the later instant.
witness.observer: A persistence test or operator sees a different `marked_at` for the same history.

open_points.subject: A2 photo modification time
open_points.text: A modification time is an absolute instant converted to UTC.
open_points.question: During one preparation or delivery, is the file modification time read exactly once and reused for camera-time validation and fallback, or may it be read separately for those decisions?
options: Read once and use one snapshot throughout the operation
Read separately whenever validation or fallback needs it
open_points.default_guess: Read the modification time once and reuse that absolute instant throughout the operation.

witness.initial: A source has no usable camera time and initially has modification time T1.
events: Syncthing or another filesystem actor changes the modification time to T2 without changing the selected content.
The deliverer determines the fallback photo moment.
outcomes: An implementation that snapshots metadata once delivers T1.
An implementation that rereads modification time delivers T2.
witness.observer: The owner and client see a different `photo_date` for the same delivered content.

open_points.subject: A9 OSV snapshot acceptance
open_points.text: Before each deployment every distribution installed in the image is checked against a snapshot of the OSV database, ecosystem PyPI, that the deployment route accepts as current. That route owns the age limit, and no code of this service reads it.
open_points.question: What exact maximum snapshot age, reference instant, time source, and boundary condition make the OSV snapshot current enough to admit deployment?
options: A fixed service policy with an explicit maximum age and inclusive boundary
A shared Factory policy whose exact symbol and value are named
An opaque decision made independently by each deployment route
open_points.default_guess: Use a named Factory policy constant, measure age once at deployment-check start using the Factory's UTC clock, and reject when age exceeds the stated maximum.

witness.initial: The deployment image passes all vulnerability matches, but its OSV snapshot has an age close to an unstated limit.
events: A deployer submits the image through the Factory deployment route.
The route evaluates whether the snapshot is current.
outcomes: One careful implementation accepts a 48-hour-old snapshot.
Another careful implementation refuses the same deployment because it permits at most 24 hours.
witness.observer: The deployer sees the image admitted by one implementation and refused by the other.

open_points.subject: A9 dependency advisory policy
open_points.text: Before each deployment every distribution installed in the image is checked against a snapshot of the OSV database, ecosystem PyPI, that the deployment route accepts as current. That route owns the age limit, and no code of this service reads it.
open_points.rule: Такая политика законна, только если её `kind` перечислен в декларации фабрики `tools/gate_rules_reads.py` (`GATE_RULES_READS`: гейт, функция, которая читает политику, и поля, которые она читает).
open_points.question: The passage must identify a gate policy whose `kind`, reader function, read fields, and applicable modules are declared in `GATE_RULES_READS`, or keep the advisory rule outside the generated specification as a deployment design fact.
